summary: A Rotary Foundation fellowship for experienced peace and development professionals, for study at Rotary Peace Centers hosted by partner universities. It has two tracks: a master's degree (15 to 24 months, with a self-designed field study) and a one-year professional development certificate for working professionals. The fellowship pays specific costs (listed under benefits), and applicants also apply separately to the host university.
eligibility_notes:
Master's track. You need a bachelor's degree with strong academic results, proficiency in English, and at least three years of full-time work experience, which the Duke-UNC and Bradford pages describe as relevant peace or development work. There must be at least three years between completing your most recent degree and the start of the fellowship, and you must not be enrolled in a degree programme. Bradford also asks for a strong commitment to international understanding and peace, shown through academic, professional and community work.

You cannot be placed at a centre in your home country: Uppsala says applicants cannot hold citizenship or permanent residence in the country where the centre is located, and the Duke-UNC and Bradford pages say you may not be placed at a centre in your home country. The fellowship is open to applicants from all over the world.

Language tests differ by centre. Bradford asks for IELTS 6.0 overall with no part below 5.5, or an equivalent. The University of Queensland asks non-native speakers for TOEFL iBT 87 (with at least 21 in writing and 19 in each other part), IELTS 6.5 with no section below 6, PTE Academic 64 with at least 60 in each part, or CES 176 with at least 169 in each section; it exempts people who completed a bachelor's or master's degree taught in English within five years before study, or who worked at least three years full time in a mainly English-speaking professional setting in designated countries. ICU describes its ideal candidate as having TOEFL iBT 79 or higher or IELTS 6.5 or higher, a clear research topic, and experience living across cultures or languages.

Other Rotary rules, carried over from stored data and not re-read on the Rotary site: active Rotary members and employees of Rotary entities are not eligible (Rotaract-only members are), and former certificate fellows or Global Grant scholars must wait three years.

Certificate track. Makerere's centre page describes the ideal candidate as a proven peace and development leader with at least five years of relevant work experience who brings a social change initiative; it points to a separate eligibility document that I could not read. Rotary's own page, which has the full certificate rules, could not be opened (see fetch problems).
age_experience_notes: Master's: at least three years of full-time relevant (peace or development) work, and a gap of at least three years between your latest degree and the fellowship start. Certificate: at least five years of relevant work per the Makerere centre page. No age limit is stated on the pages read.
funding_summary: The fellowship covers specific components rather than every cost. The partner pages list: tuition and university fees; a monthly stipend for living costs including room and board; round-trip transportation between home and study place at the start and end; a contingency fund; funds for conferences and research; and support for the field study or internship. ICU also lists the application fee and admission fee. Master's study lasts 15 months (Bradford), 18 months (Queensland) or about 22 months to two years (ICU), and Duke-UNC describes a two- to three-month self-designed field experience; the certificate lasts one year.
programmes_note: Master's degrees in peace and conflict studies and related development fields at the Rotary Peace Centers: Duke-UNC (Master of International Development Policy at Duke; social science and public health master's at UNC such as global studies, public health, education, journalism and social work), International Christian University (master's in peace studies), University of Bradford (seven MA and MSc options), University of Queensland (Master of Peace and Conflict Studies) and Uppsala University (Master's Programme in Peace and Conflict Studies). The certificate is a separate one-year blended programme for working professionals; Makerere University in Uganda hosts the Advanced Certificate in Peacebuilding, Conflict Transformation and Development. ICU's page says three centres offer certificates, but I could verify only Makerere.
institutions_note: Master's partners: Duke University with the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (USA), International Christian University (Japan), University of Bradford (England), University of Queensland (Australia), Uppsala University (Sweden). Certificate: Makerere University (Uganda) was verified; other certificate centres were not. The partner pages call the network seven or eight centres. You rank two master's centres and one certificate centre on the Rotary form, then apply separately to the university if selected.

summary.detail: Master's degree at one of five partner universities. Length: Bradford 15 months (September coursework, summer field experience, dissertation to December of the following year); Queensland 18 months, starting in February with an 8 to 12 week field experience; ICU about 22 months to two years; Duke-UNC a two- to three-month self-designed field experience. Selection for the fellowship does not guarantee admission to the university.

application_steps.title: Check eligibility and choose centres
application_steps.detail: Read the eligibility rules on the Rotary application platform, then research the centres and rank two master's centres and one certificate centre. The application for the 2028-29 fellowship opens online in February 2027.

application_steps.title: Submit the Rotary application by mid-May
application_steps.detail: Submit the application with your resume, recommendations and essays, plus transcripts and test scores for the master's track. Rotary's partner pages say applications close in mid-May (15 May in earlier cycles); the closing date for 2028-29 is not given on the pages I could read.

application_steps.title: Connect with a local Rotary club
application_steps.detail: The Bradford page calls this optional but strongly recommended. The Bradford and ICU pages also describe an endorsement or application route through a local Rotary district, which Queensland's page does not mention; check the Rotary form for the current rule.

application_steps.title: Rotary reviews and selects fellows
application_steps.detail: Fellowships are awarded on a highly competitive basis. At Queensland, applications are reviewed from July to October and applicants are notified from late October to early November; Bradford says results are emailed in November. Uppsala's page says its centre director selects its fellows. The scoring criteria are not described on these pages.

application_steps.title: Apply to the host university
application_steps.detail: If selected, you apply separately for admission to the master's programme at the host university (for example Bradford, Uppsala or Queensland), and later arrange a student visa. Selection for the fellowship does not guarantee admission.

application_steps.title: Study, complete the field experience and fulfil fellow duties
application_steps.detail: At Queensland fellows organise their own field placement, present at the annual seminar in the final semester and join an annual visit to Canberra; fellows must do the compulsory academic, service and field activities. Duke-UNC fellows design a field experience of two to three months.

fetch_problems: Rotary's own pages on the peace fellowships (the master's page, the main page and the apply page) returned a 'verifying your browser' check and HTTP 429. I did not try to get around it. The content comes from the partner universities' pages only.
One ICU address (the special-programme index page) returned 403; the other ICU page and the ICU Rotary Peace Center apply page were readable.
The Uppsala programme page and the Uppsala checklist PDF were not read (404 or not opened).
notes: Not re-confirmed from Rotary, carried over from stored data: 'up to 50 master's and up to 120 certificate fellowships a year'. Partner pages give different totals (up to 130 fellowships a year on the Duke, UNC and Makerere pages; up to 170 on the Queensland and Bradford pages; about 10 master's fellows each at Bradford, ICU and Duke-UNC). Editors should check the number on Rotary's page.

Not re-confirmed from Rotary, carried over from stored data: the rules on active Rotary members, employees of Rotary entities, Rotaract-only members, and the three-year wait for former certificate fellows or Global Grant scholars.

Partner pages disagree on some details. The ICU page gives the programme as two years in one place and 22 months in another. The Bradford page lists district endorsement and an interview; Queensland says to apply through the Rotary portal. The network is described as seven or eight centres. Bradford's page gives the eligibility experience as three years while Makerere's certificate page gives five years for the certificate track.
The stored text 'Master's programmes last 15 to 24 months with a two- to three-month self-designed field study' matches the Makerere page, which compares the master's track in these words.
The stored funding_type 'full' should be reviewed: the benefits above list the named components; the pages read do not state an amount for the stipend or say health insurance is paid.
